summary: The Android release publisher now uses GitHub Releases. Six local contract tests pass; GitHub Actions CI run #45 also completed its Windows job successfully, which runs the publisher tests before Flutter tests, analysis and Windows Release build. A real Android tag release and its three APK assets have not yet been exercised.

checks.name: Publisher contract and retry tests
checks.observation: All six tests pass using a mocked GitVerse API. Tests verify multipart attachment, a bounded 15-minute request timeout, transient retry, reconciling an accepted upload after a lost response, skipping an already-present same-size asset, rejecting conflicting assets and failing closed without RELEASE_API_KEY.

checks.name: JavaScript syntax, workflow YAML and diff checks
checks.command: node --check scripts/android_release/publish.mjs && node --check scripts/android_release/publish.test.mjs; Ruby YAML parse for both Android Release and Flutter Windows CI workflows; git diff --check
checks.observation: Both workflow files parse as YAML, JavaScript syntax checks pass and the diff has no whitespace errors.

checks.name: GitHub Windows runner publisher, Flutter tests, analyzer and Release build
checks.command: GitHub Actions CI run #45 · windows job
checks.observation: Windows job completed successfully on commit 0d7f3a3. The workflow step order runs scripts/android_release/publish*.test.mjs before Flutter tests, analyzer and Windows Release compilation. The overall CI run's separate Flutter job was still in progress when inspected.

checks.name: Published Android 1.0.17 GitHub release
checks.observation: No release tag was pushed and no public release or APK asset was created by this change.

remaining: When the Android release is authorized, trigger the tag workflow for the current version and verify that the public GitHub release lists all three signed ABI APKs. Keep publication open until all assets are confirmed.
